描述_EN: from surviving mamluk textiles, it seems that blue was a favoured colour. similar textiles have not been found in china and it is possible that these silks were made specially for the mamluk empire (1250-1517). mamluk and other textiles from the islamic world are known to incorporate scripts into their designs, so the inclusion of a longevity ideograph may have been a deliberate move. there are stitch holes along the selvedge while opposite there are remains of stitches in red silk. a small piece of linen cloth (unbleached) is attached to one edge. this is contained within a circle around which are curly cloud shapes. this fragment of silk damask have a pattern in blue on a yellow ground showing a simplified chinese symbol resembling the shou character for longevity. the weaving may have been carried out in china and the silks then exported westwards, or it could have been done outside china by islamic craftsmen familiar with chinese patterning.
描述_ZN: 从现存的马穆鲁克纺织品来看，蓝色似乎是一种受欢迎的颜色。 类似的纺织品在中国没有发现，这些丝绸有可能是专门为马穆鲁克帝国（1250-1517）制作的。 马穆鲁克和其他来自伊斯兰世界的纺织品都知道将文字纳入他们的设计中，所以加入一个长寿的表意文字可能是一个有意的举动。 沿边有针孔，而对面有红绸的针脚残留。 一小块亚麻布（未漂白）连接在一个边缘。 这个图案包含在一个圆圈内，圆圈周围是卷曲的云朵形状。 这块丝绸绫罗绸缎上有一个黄底蓝字的图案，显示了一个简化的中国符号，类似于长寿的寿字。 织造可能是在中国进行的，然后丝绸向西出口，也可能是在中国以外由熟悉中国图案的伊斯兰工匠完成。
